status: Proposed fixed authorisation/recipient concept; no default-branch acceptance or clinical competence
reuseDecision: Generic safe help, hazard signs, minor-cut care, food-allergy triggers, lifestyle harm and recreational-drug categories do not establish the different authorisation/recipient model of prescription versus non-prescription medicines. Safe chemical avoidance alone does not entail medicine purpose, availability or appropriate recipient/instruction reasoning.

independentWitness.oldSuccessNewMissing: A learner knows everyday hazards/help, explains food-allergy reactions and correct minor-care, and classifies alcohol/nicotine effects but thinks all pharmacy medicines are interchangeable or that OTC medicines have no rules. Those whole closest cards can pass while the new model fails.
independentWitness.newSuccessWithoutOld: A learner correctly explains the known prescription/OTC cards and the changed sharing/uncertainty cases but cannot explain liver/lung drug harms, hallucinogen categories, allergy/intolerance or minor-wound care. Those independent families are not hard prerequisites.
independentWitness.minimalGrain: One authorisation/appropriate-use conceptual model, not a medicine-administration skill or separate node per drug/product/grade. Risk and adult-help application discriminate understanding of that model.

guideStatus: Complete original untested low-confidence design. Checked sources support specific content, not activity efficacy.
